title: Online Assessments (OA) Check
description: Predict how remaining time in a fixed OA window should change your pacing strategy.

questions.prompt: What is a defining trait of a HackerRank-hosted Online Assessment (OA)?

options.text: It can be paused and resumed at any time
It runs inside one fixed time window that typically can't be paused
It has no time limit at all
It only contains multiple-choice questions

questions.explanation: OAs run against a single countdown for the whole session, usually without the ability to pause.

questions.prompt: With thresholds rush (<15 min), pace (<45 min), plan (>=45 min), what mode applies at exactly 45 minutes remaining?

options.text: rush
pace
plan
None — 45 is an invalid boundary

questions.explanation: 45 minutes is the first value that reaches the plan threshold, since pace only covers values strictly below 45.

questions.prompt: Why does pacing mode change as time runs out during an OA?

options.text: Because effort should stay proportional to time remaining, favoring partial credit late on
Because HackerRank penalizes fast submissions
Because later questions are always easier
Pacing mode has no real effect on outcome

questions.explanation: Treating minute 5 like minute 80 wastes the fixed clock; late-window strategy should favor banking partial credit.

questions.prompt: In `rush` mode with a question you can't fully solve, what's the recommended move?

options.text: Skip it and submit nothing
Submit whatever passes the most visible test cases for partial credit
Restart the whole OA
Wait for the timer to expire

questions.explanation: Since grading is per test case, submitting a partial solution still banks credit even under time pressure.

questions.prompt: Does the rush/pace/plan idea only apply to HackerRank OAs specifically?

options.text: Yes, it's a HackerRank-exclusive feature
No, it generalizes to any timed, multi-question test with a fixed window
Yes, it only works for coding questions, never multiple choice
No, it only applies to certifications

questions.explanation: The pacing strategy is a general timed-test tactic, not something specific to HackerRank's implementation.
